---
title: "Variable selection"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5,
                      dpi = 96)
```

A measure carries a risk-adjustment set of tens to hundreds of candidate
variables. Which of them the model should keep is a selection problem,
and it has one feature that ordinary penalized regression does not handle:
the provider effects must stay in the model, unpenalized, while the risk
factors are selected. Selecting on a pooled model (without provider
effects) inflates the false discoveries, because the omitted provider
effect acts as a confounder shared by every risk factor correlated with
it.

`var_select()` fits the lasso or group-lasso path of the fixed-effect
model with the provider effects kept, for binary, binomial, continuous and
survival outcomes; `cv()` chooses the penalty by cross-validation.

## The objective

$$-\frac{1}{n}\,\ell(\gamma, \beta) + \lambda \sum_j m_j |\beta_j|
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
-\frac{1}{n}\,\ell(\gamma, \beta) + \lambda \sum_g m_g \|\beta_g\|_2 ,$$

with the provider effects $\gamma$ never penalized. The path is solved by
coordinate descent on standardized covariates (each group orthonormalized)
with one Newton step on the provider effects per cycle, warm starts along
a decreasing sequence of $\lambda$ and an active-set strategy, so that the
provider effects are updated in closed form from their own records and
never form indicator columns (the multi-layer algorithm of the KECC
measures paper; `grplasso`'s `pp.lasso` and `grp.lasso`). The linear model
needs no step on the provider effects at all (see Continuous outcomes).

## A lasso path

```{r}
library(pprof)
d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 60, n_covariates = 8, beta = c(0.6, -0.5, 0.4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
              seed = 4)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = paste0("x", 1:8), provider = "provider", patient = "patient",
              message = FALSE)
path <- var_select(pd, n_lambda = 30)
path
plot(path)
```

* `penalize`: the covariates that carry a penalty (default all); the
  others, a committee's mandatory adjusters say, enter unpenalized.
* `multiplier`: per-covariate (or per-group) penalty multipliers.
* `lambda`, `n_lambda`, `lambda_min_ratio`: the penalty sequence; by
  default 100 values from the smallest $\lambda$ with every penalized
  coefficient zero down to $10^{-4}$ times it.

The coefficients at any penalty, and the selected set:

```{r}
coef(path, lambda = path$lambda[12])$beta
selected_covariates(path, which = c(8, 15, 30))
```

## Group lasso

A categorical risk factor coded as several 0/1 columns should enter or
leave the model as a whole. Give each covariate a group label (0 for an
unpenalized covariate); the penalty on a group is $\sqrt{\text{size}}$
times the group norm by default.

```{r}
grp <- var_select(pd, penalty = "group_lasso", group = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 0, 4), n_lambda = 30)
grp
selected_covariates(grp, which = 15)
```

## Choosing the penalty: cross-validation

`cv()` refits the path on every training fold and scores the held-out
rows by the binomial deviance (the partial-likelihood deviance per event
for the Cox model, the person-period deviance for the discrete-time
model). Folds are formed **within every provider** over its patients, so
that each provider is present in every training set; a provider held out
entirely is predicted with the median provider effect.

```{r}
cvp <- cv(path, n_folds = 5, seed = 1)
cvp
plot(cvp)
cvp$selected_min
cvp$selected_1se
```

`lambda_min` is the penalty with the smallest cross-validated deviance,
`lambda_1se` the largest penalty within one standard error of it (fewer
variables). For selecting risk adjusters, the measure development work of
the KECC measures uses `lambda_min` and then refits the fixed-effect model
on the selected set:

```{r}
pd_sel <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = cvp$selected_min, provider = "provider",
                  patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
summary(fit_logistic_fe(pd_sel))
```

## Continuous outcomes

For a continuous outcome the model is the linear model $y_{ij} = \gamma_i +
Z_{ij}^\top\beta + \varepsilon_{ij}$ with the squared-error loss
$\frac{1}{2n}\sum (y - \gamma - Z\beta)^2$. Here the provider effects
need no iteration: for any $\beta$ the best $\gamma_i$ is the provider's
mean of $y - Z\beta$, so they are profiled out in closed form by centring
the outcome and the covariates within providers, and the path is coordinate
descent on $\beta$ alone over the Gram matrix of the centred data. The end
of a long path is the within-provider regression of `fit_linear_fe()`;
`cv()` scores the held-out squared error.

```{r}
dc <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 60, type = "continuous", n_covariates = 6,
               beta = c(0.6, -0.5, 0.4, 0, 0, 0), seed = 5)
pdc <- pp_data(dc, y = "y", x = paste0("x", 1:6), provider = "provider",
               patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
lin_path <- var_select(pdc, n_lambda = 30)
lin_cv <- cv(lin_path, n_folds = 5, seed = 1)
lin_cv$selected_min
```

## Survival outcomes

On a survival `pp_data()` object the same calls fit:

* `model = "cox"` (default): the Cox model stratified by provider (its
  baselines absorb the provider effects), with counting-process rows,
  weights and offsets as in `fit_cox()`; the cross-validation loss is the
  partial-likelihood deviance of the held-out rows within their own strata.
* `model = "discrete"`: the discrete-time hazard model
  $\mathrm{logit}\, h_{jk} = \alpha_k + \gamma_i + Z_j^\top\beta$, with
  the periods the distinct event times, one row per subject (no `start`),
  unpenalized period and provider effects and the lasso on $\beta$. The
  likelihood is computed without expanding the data into person-periods.
  The provider effects are identified by a zero median.

```{r}
s <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 40, rows_per_patient = c(1, 1), type = "survival",
              n_covariates = 6, beta = c(0.6, -0.5, 0.4, 0, 0, 0), seed = 41)
ps <- pp_data(s, x = paste0("x", 1:6), provider = "provider", patient = "patient",
              time = "stop", event = "event", cutoff = 0, message = FALSE)
cox_path <- var_select(ps, n_lambda = 20)
selected_covariates(cox_path, which = 20)
s$stop <- ceiling(s$stop * 12) / 12   # monthly periods
psm <- pp_data(s, x = paste0("x", 1:6), provider = "provider", patient = "patient",
               time = "stop", event = "event", cutoff = 0, message = FALSE)
disc <- var_select(psm, model = "discrete", n_lambda = 20)
disc
```

At the smallest penalty of a long path the coefficients approach those of
the unpenalized model: `survival::coxph()` with `strata(provider)` for the
Cox model, a logistic regression on the expanded person-period data with
period and provider indicators for the discrete-time model.

## References

Breheny P, Huang J (2015). Group descent algorithms for nonconvex
penalized linear and logistic regression models with grouped predictors.
*Statistics and Computing*, 25, 173-187.

Friedman J, Hastie T, Tibshirani R (2010). Regularization paths for
generalized linear models via coordinate descent. *Journal of Statistical
Software*, 33(1), 1-22.
